title: Adding up with SUM
summary: Write your first addition formula, then use the SUM function with a range, and let the result update by itself when the data changes.
intro:
Every formula in Excel starts with `=`. You can add cells with the plus sign, such as `=B2+B3+B4`, but that gets long when there are many cells.

The `SUM` function adds up a whole range in a short formula: `=SUM(B2:B6)`. The result stays right whenever a value in the range changes, so never type the total yourself.

faq.q: What is the difference between `=B2+B3` and `=SUM(B2:B3)`?
faq.a: The result is the same, but `SUM` is shorter and easier with long ranges, and it ignores text inside the range.

faq.q: Why not just type the total?
faq.a: A typed number does not change when the data changes, while a formula recalculates automatically.

first-formula.prompt: These are the quantities a bakery sold in one day. Every formula starts with `=`. Select cell `B7`, type `=B2+B3+B4+B5+B6`, then press Enter.
first-formula.hint: Start with `=`, then type the cell names with `+` between them.

sum-function.prompt: The quicker way is the `SUM` function. You put the range you want to add inside its brackets. In `B7`, type the formula `=SUM(B2:B6)`.
sum-function.hint: The range `B2:B6` means every cell from `B2` to `B6`.

pick-the-range.prompt: You don't have to type the range yourself. Type `=SUM(` in cell `B7`, then drag over the cells from `B2` to `B6` (or tap them one after another), then type `)` and press Enter.
pick-the-range.hint: After you type the bracket `(`, Excel inserts the name of any cell you click into the formula.

no-hard-coding.prompt: 30 more pies were sold, so the quantity in `B4` is now 120. Don't type the total yourself: in `B7`, write a formula that adds up the quantities, so the result updates by itself whenever the data changes.
no-hard-coding.hint: If you type 450 directly, the result won't change when the quantities do. Use `SUM` with the range.

part-of-a-column.prompt: The baker wants the total of bread, cakes and pies only. In `D2`, write a formula that adds up the range `B2:B4`.
part-of-a-column.hint: The range starts at `B2` and ends at `B4`.

read-a-sum.prompt: On this sheet, what is the result of `=SUM(B2:B3)`?
read-a-sum.hint: The formula adds only the two cells `B2` and `B3`.
